description: Fixture corpus for the version 1 platform foundation: the event envelope of docs/EVENTS.md section 2 with the organisation, project and durable-job payloads this source owns, the project event-stream control messages of docs/API.md section 18.1, and the refusal body of docs/API.md section 5. Valid cases must decode and re-encode to the byte string recorded in canonical.json; invalid cases must be refused with the recorded reason. Both languages run this manifest, which is what makes the TypeScript control plane and any Go consumer one implementation rather than two that happen to agree today.

valid.name: organisation-created
valid.note: The first event a deployment records. It has no project_id, because an organisation precedes any project association, and the envelope makes that member optional for exactly this case.

valid.name: project-created
valid.note: The event a project's stream begins at. The slug is recorded as a mutable alias beside the identifier, never instead of it (docs/DOMAIN_MODEL.md section 3).

valid.name: project-updated
valid.note: Names the fields that changed rather than restating the record: current state is queryable, and the audit question is what moved.

valid.name: project-repository-changed
valid.note: Both sides of a repository move, in the provider-agnostic canonical form of docs/DOMAIN_MODEL.md section 6. The new value carries a non-default port, which is what a self-hosted forge looks like and what a normaliser that only understands github.com would get wrong.

valid.name: project-archived
valid.note: Previous and new state, which docs/EVENTS.md section 8 requires of a state change.

valid.name: user-invited
valid.note: The install token an operator mints at first run. The actor is the command line rather than a human, because no human has authenticated yet; the payload states when the way in closes and never what it is.

valid.name: user-credentials-set
valid.note: The administrator bootstrap of docs/SECURITY.md section 6.1, recorded on the organisation stream because no project exists yet. It names the user and the route the credential arrived by, and carries nothing derived from the credential.

valid.name: authentication-login-succeeded
valid.note: A password login. It names the session it issued, so a later session.revoked can be matched to it.

valid.name: authentication-login-failed
valid.note: A refused attempt. The actor is system rather than the user, because an unauthenticated attempt has not established who made it; the payload names the user only because this attempt reached an existing account.

valid.name: session-revoked
valid.note: Sign-out. Rotation and administrative revocation are the same event with a different reason, which is what lets an operator read a session's whole life from one stream.

valid.name: job-enqueued
valid.note: Durable work accepted. It is written in the same transaction as the state change that scheduled it, so the audit trail cannot show one without the other.

valid.name: job-succeeded
valid.note: A completed job, with the attempt count so a retry that eventually worked is distinguishable from a first-time success.

valid.name: job-failed-retrying
valid.note: A failed attempt that will be retried. retrying is stated rather than inferred, so an operator can tell a retry from a dead job without reading the runner's source.

valid.name: stream-subscribe
valid.note: The resume request of docs/API.md section 18.1: the last sequence the client applied, and the largest replay it is willing to receive.

valid.name: stream-subscribed
valid.note: Acceptance stating the current sequence and the oldest replayable one, so a client knows before any event whether its position is inside the window.

valid.name: stream-refresh-required
valid.note: The explicit refresh instruction of docs/EVENTS.md section 10. A silent jump would leave the client quietly wrong.

valid.name: stream-heartbeat
valid.note: Liveness on a quiet project, carrying the sequence so a missed event is detectable without waiting for the next one.

valid.name: stream-error
valid.note: A refusal on an open subscription. Refusals that precede the upgrade are HTTP responses instead, so an unauthorised subscriber never obtains a socket.

valid.name: api-error-version-conflict
valid.note: The exact body docs/API.md section 5 prints, including details.current_version so a caller can re-read and retry rather than guess.

valid.name: api-error-not-found
valid.note: A refusal with no details. The member is absent rather than null, so a consumer testing for the key gets the same answer whichever handler produced it.

valid.name: api-error-paginated-meta
valid.note: meta carries next_cursor on a refusal as well as on a success, because meta is one shape (section 6).

valid.name: connector-enrolled
valid.note: An enrolment token was redeemed and a device identity issued. The token identifier is recorded and the token is not: an event is append-only (docs/EVENTS.md section 8).

valid.name: connector-connected
valid.note: The connector's first authenticated channel moved it out of PENDING_ENROLMENT. Both sides of the transition are named.

valid.name: connector-degraded
valid.note: A conclusion drawn from silence, so the payload states how long the silence had lasted and the actor is system rather than the connector.

valid.name: connector-disconnected
valid.note: The disconnect threshold was exceeded, which is why the trigger is heartbeat_timeout rather than channel_closed.

valid.name: connector-revoked
valid.note: Revocation reached the channels, the routes and the sessions, and the payload records how much of each, because docs/CONNECTOR_PROTOCOL.md section 18 makes revocation all of those at once.

valid.name: workspace-observed
valid.note: Bounded Git context recorded against a project stream: a display label and a path hash rather than a path, and no changed-file list.

valid.name: workspace-head-changed
valid.note: Both sides of the move, because a review captured before it was captured against the previous head.

invalid.name: event-unknown-type
invalid.note: review.created is a real event type, owned by schemas/review/v1.schema.json. This codec refuses it rather than decoding it into a shape it does not define.

invalid.name: event-unsupported-schema-version
invalid.note: A future envelope version is refused outright rather than best-effort parsed.

invalid.name: event-sequence-zero
invalid.note: A project stream starts at 1. Zero is the value a subscriber sends to mean it holds nothing, and it is never an event's position.

invalid.name: event-unknown-property
invalid.note: additionalProperties: false on the envelope is what stops a tenant hint, a header or a credential riding along beside the documented members.

invalid.name: event-actor-unknown-type
invalid.note: The actor vocabulary of docs/EVENTS.md section 5 is closed. Actor identity is never inferred, and never invented.

invalid.name: event-payload-unknown-property
invalid.note: docs/EVENTS.md section 8 forbids raw secrets and authorisation headers in a payload. A closed payload schema is what makes that a property of the audit trail rather than of a code review.

invalid.name: event-login-failed-carries-identifier
invalid.note: A failed login must not record what was submitted. People type passwords into email fields, and an append-only table is the worst place to find out; the closed payload schema is what makes that impossible rather than merely discouraged.

invalid.name: event-identifier-out-of-class
invalid.note: An identifier is bounded by length and character class. The prefix is never checked, and a space is never inside the class.

invalid.name: stream-unknown-type
invalid.note: An unrecognised control message is refused rather than ignored, so a client speaking a later dialect learns that it is doing so.

invalid.name: stream-subscribe-negative-sequence
invalid.note: A resume position below zero has no meaning, and accepting it would make the replay bound arithmetic answer a nonsense question.

invalid.name: api-error-unknown-code
invalid.note: The code vocabulary is closed on the producing side. A client MUST tolerate a code it does not know; a server MUST NOT invent one.

invalid.name: api-error-unknown-detail
invalid.note: details is a fixed vocabulary rather than a free object, which is what stops a handler attaching a cookie or a request body to a refusal.

invalid.name: event-connector-enrolled-carries-the-token
invalid.note: The enrolment payload has no member capable of carrying the token, so the refusal is the schema's rather than a reviewer's.

invalid.name: event-workspace-observed-carries-a-path
invalid.note: A full filesystem path cannot be smuggled through display_path: the pattern refuses path separators.

invalid.name: event-connector-degraded-self-reported
invalid.note: A connector cannot report itself degraded: heartbeat is not in the degraded trigger vocabulary, because a silent connector reports nothing.
